result.journal: Proc. ACM Meas. Anal. Comput. Syst.
result.keywords: Datacenter operators need efficient methods to diagnose anomalous network behavior and performance stragglers across large clusters. This article presents Merlin, a causal sketching framework that combines interpretable statistical inference with lightweight traffic measurement to identify root causes from job traces and packet-level summaries. The approach targets large-scale production environments, supports both per-flow and aggregate analysis, and emphasizes low-overhead deployment, unbiased diagnosis, and practical tradeoffs between accuracy and space. Experiments on warehouse-scale traces and distributed analytics workloads illustrate how the framework can help isolate bottlenecks, contention, and misconfigured resources in modern datacenters.
result.title: Merlin: Causal Sketching for Datacenter Traffic Anomaly Diagnosis.
